etymologies.heading: Etymology 1
paragraphs: First attested in 1533; borrowed from Latin rūminātus, perfect active participle of rūminor (“to chew the cud, turn over in the mind”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), from rūmen (“the throat, gullet”) +‎ -ō (verb-forming suffix), itself of uncertain origin.
senses: (intransitive) To chew cud. (Said of ruminants.) Involves regurgitating partially digested food from the rumen.

etymologies.heading: Etymology 2
paragraphs: First attested in 1800, in the writings of John Hull; borrowed from Latin rūminātus, see Etymology 1 and -ate (adjective-forming suffix).
senses: (botany) Having a hard albumen penetrated by irregular channels filled with softer matter, as the nutmeg and the seeds of the North American papaw.
